NDT training in Jackson: how it works for Jackson employers and technicians

Short answer: Jackson, Mississippi employers and technicians can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training from Atlantis NDT as live online theory combined with practical sessions onsite at the employer's facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is employer-based: the written practice sets training and experience, a Level III gives the general, specific and practical exams, and the employer certifies. Atlantis has no classroom building in Jackson; training is delivered online or at your site.

Central Mississippi's NDT demand is a mix of automotive manufacturing, specialty refining, power generation including a large nuclear station, pipelines, and the state's transport infrastructure, with the Gulf Coast shipyards and refinery a few hours south. Technicians here often travel: an outage at Port Gibson, a turnaround at Vicksburg or Pascagoula, then back to plant work around Jackson. That makes a fixed classroom schedule hard to keep. Employer-site and blended training fit the way central Mississippi crews actually work.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Jackson

Every course follows SNT-TC-1A with content aligned to ANSI/ASNT CP-105 and can be taken live online, onsite in the Jackson metro, or blended. Here is how each method maps to central Mississippi work.

For a crew mixing plant and outage work, UT, VT and MT are the usual starting point, with ET and RT added for power plants and pipelines. Request a Jackson training quote and tell us what your crew inspects.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Jackson, step by step

  1. Check the written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies, so the written practice comes first. If yours needs creating or updating, see written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Theory for the method and level, online or onsite. Required hours are in the written practice; recommended minimums are in the requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised production or outage inspection, logged and signed.
  4. General examination. Method principles, written.
  5. Specific examination. Your equipment, procedures and acceptance standards, for example ASME Section V and B31.3 at a refinery, API 1104 on a pipeline or AWS D1.1 in a structural shop.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on testing of specimens with known flaws, graded in person by a Level III.
  7. Vision examination. Near vision and colour contrast, usually every year.
  8. Employer certification. Signed by the employer on the Level III's recommendation.
  9. Recertification. On the schedule set in the written practice.

More on the employer programme: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Jackson crews

Atlantis does not run a training centre in Jackson or anywhere in Mississippi. Training reaches your crew three ways:

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory in real time, with sessions arranged around shifts and travel. It covers the formal-training component only; see NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. A Level III-led course at your plant or shop in Jackson, Canton, Clinton, Pearl, Flowood, Vicksburg or wherever your work is, using your instruments and procedures.
  • Blended. Online theory, then a concentrated practical block at your site; good for companies whose technicians are out on jobs most weeks.

Refueling outages at the nuclear station, spring and autumn fossil outages and refinery turnarounds set the rhythm for central Mississippi contractors. We plan cohorts outside those windows. Ask about onsite training for your Jackson crew; cohort and onsite quotes arrive within one business day.

Companies with technicians across Mississippi, Louisiana and Alabama can use corporate NDT training to run one programme with shared records and Level III oversight.

Where NDT technicians work in Jackson

  • Automotive manufacturing. Vehicle assembly in Canton and tyre manufacturing in Clinton, plus their suppliers, use MT, PT, VT and UT for tooling, fixtures, welded structures and plant equipment, along with maintenance inspection on boilers and compressed-air systems.
  • Specialty refining. Refining based in Jackson with operations at Vicksburg, and the large Gulf Coast refinery at Pascagoula, need piping and vessel inspection with API and ASME code context, especially during turnarounds.
  • Power and nuclear. The utility headquartered in Jackson and the nuclear station at Port Gibson create outage demand for UT, ET, VT and RT technicians. Nuclear work is typically governed by additional programme requirements; many nuclear licensees qualify NDT personnel to ASNT CP-189 rather than SNT-TC-1A, so check before you commit.
  • Shipbuilding. Naval and commercial shipbuilding on the Gulf Coast at Pascagoula employs large NDT departments working to NAVSEA and ABS requirements, and many central Mississippi technicians spend time there.
  • Pipelines and gas storage. Major interstate natural gas pipelines and underground storage facilities in Mississippi need RT and UT for construction and integrity work under API 1104 and ASME B31.8.
  • Aviation. Military airlift operations at the Jackson airport and aviation maintenance across the state use PT, ET and VT under aerospace and military specifications.
  • Bridges and transport. The Mississippi Department of Transportation is headquartered in Jackson, and steel bridges across the state, including the Mississippi River crossings at Vicksburg and Natchez, need VT, MT and UT on fracture-critical members.

Radiography licensing in Mississippi

Mississippi is an NRC Agreement State, and radioactive-material licensing is handled by the Mississippi State Department of Health, Division of Radiological Health, which also registers radiation-producing machines such as industrial X-ray equipment. A Jackson RT company holds the state licence; its radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the training and certification requirements in the state's radiation rules, which mirror the NRC industrial radiography framework: radiation safety training, recognised radiographer certification, personal dosimetry, survey meters and two-person crews at temporary job sites. Out-of-state crews generally need reciprocity before working in Mississippi.

Our RT courses cover technique, exposure, interpretation and radiation safety principles for SNT-TC-1A certification. They do not authorise anyone to use sources; that authority comes from the licensee and the Division of Radiological Health.

Method spotlight: eddy current testing of heat-exchanger and condenser tubing

Outage work at central Mississippi power plants and refineries puts a premium on technicians who can inspect tubing. Condensers, feedwater heaters and process heat exchangers contain thousands of tubes, and eddy current testing with bobbin probes is the standard way to screen them quickly for wall loss, pitting, cracking and fretting at support plates.

An ET Level II for this kind of work covers:

  • Bobbin-probe fundamentals: fill factor, differential and absolute channels, and frequency selection for the tube material and wall thickness.
  • Calibration standards with machined flaws, and building phase-angle curves to estimate flaw depth.
  • Recognising support plates, baffles, dents and deposits so they are not mistaken for defects.
  • Limits of bobbin probes on ferromagnetic tubes, and when other techniques are needed.
  • Data recording and tube-sheet mapping so that plugging decisions are traceable.

Be aware that nuclear stations frequently qualify tubing analysts under their own nuclear-specific programmes; SNT-TC-1A ET certification is the right foundation for fossil plants, refineries and chemical plants, and a useful base for further nuclear qualification. Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator gives trainees 12 NDT methods across 5 3D environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Use it to rehearse set-ups and scanning between online theory and the onsite practical. Local details are on Practical NDT in Jackson, MS.

It is practice only. The simulator does not count as OJT and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens graded by a Level III.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who builds the course content, oversees practical sessions and examinations, and works with employers on written practices and certification records.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Jackson

How do I get NDT certified in Jackson, MS?

Complete formal training in a method, gain documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given or approved by a Level III, pass a vision test, and be certified by your employer under its SNT-TC-1A written practice. Atlantis provides the training and can support exams and the written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Mississippi?

Theory, yes, through live online classes that meet the formal-training requirement. Practical training and the practical exam must be done in person, onsite with your employer or at an arranged location. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice, whether you hold UT Level I and how quickly you build documented experience. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are in the training requirements matrix; employers can require more, and experience usually takes longer than classroom training.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Mississippi?

The employer needs a licence from the Mississippi State Department of Health's Division of Radiological Health, and radiographers and assistants must meet the state's training and certification requirements before using sources. An NDT course on its own is not a licence.

What does NDT training cost in Jackson?

It depends on methods, levels, group size, delivery format and whether exams or written-practice support are included, so we quote each request. Request a Jackson training quote and receive cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Jackson employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the standard US reference for NDT personnel qualification and is widely used in manufacturing, refining, pipelines and fossil power. Nuclear and naval work often add further requirements. Certification is employer-specific, so a new employer recertifies you, but your training and experience records go with you.

Can you train our crew at our plant in Canton or Vicksburg?

Yes. Onsite delivery anywhere in central Mississippi is standard for employer cohorts, scheduled around your production and outage calendar.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training in Mississippi?

Those programmes require approved providers. GI Bill benefits apply to programmes approved for VA education benefits, and WIOA training funds generally require a provider on the state's Eligible Training Provider List, accessed in Mississippi through WIN Job Centers. Atlantis does not claim either approval. With us, the practical route is employer-paid training; if you want to use benefits, ask an approved college programme.

Does SNT-TC-1A certification qualify me for nuclear outage work?

Not automatically. Many nuclear licensees use ASNT CP-189 or their own programme requirements, with plant-specific training and exams. SNT-TC-1A certification and documented experience are a strong foundation, but confirm the plant's requirements with the contractor that is hiring.

Which methods should I start with in central Mississippi?

UT, VT and MT cover most plant and fabrication work; ET is valuable for outage tube inspection, and RT for pipelines and shipyards. See the NDT salary guide for how level and method affect pay.

Do you offer API 570 or CWI courses?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some refinery and fabrication employers also ask for API inspector or AWS CWI credentials; those are separate schemes, and we can explain how they fit with SNT-TC-1A.

Can Atlantis prepare me for ASNT Level III?

Yes, covering the Basic exam, method exams and the practical side of writing procedures and administering exams. See ASNT Level III training.
